column3: He poured water into the glass until it was full.
column4: Swap test: "in" works identically; "into" requires direction/motion shown here

column3: This coffee has less sugar than yesterday's drink.
column4: Grammar: "the drink yesterday" is not standard English; needs possessive or "from"

column3: She made a cake from scratch using butter and eggs.
column4: Swap test: "baked" fits identically; clarify unique sense of "made"

column3: The meeting lasted two hours and was very productive.
column4: Grammar: "was productive today" has redundant time reference; remove "today"

column3: I sent her a message about the meeting but she hasn't responded yet.
column4: Swap test: "email" or "note" fits as well; context needed to narrow it

column3: She sat in the middle of the room where everyone could see her.
column4: Grammar: "where everyone saw" is incomplete; needs "could see" or "see her"

column3: The new car model featured a sleek design that impressed the engineers.
column4: Ambiguity: could mean person or design; clarify which sense (דגם/דגם vs דוגמן)

column3: The monster in the movie scared the children in the theater.
column4: Grammar: "in theater" missing article; should be "in the theater"

column3: The train headed North toward the mountains in the early morning.
column4: Grammar: "early morning" needs article "in the"; awkward without preposition
